You're carrying three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. No move cleared its cost this week, so you're holding. Your bench is light—Mykolenko tops it at 3.1—but that's typical early in a season when you're trying to squeeze value into your starting eleven.

One thing worth tracking: your defence leans on last season's data for who started and how often. Gvardiol, Van Dijk and Gabriel were all reliable, but if any loses minutes over the summer, the projection won't yet reflect it. Same goes for Raya and Pope. The ranking is player quality rather than nailed-on status, so a first gameweek or two will tell you more than the model can.

Your eleven projects to 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. He is 0.3 clear of Salah as captain and carries genuine ceiling—a 25% chance of 10+—but also real floor risk, with an 8% chance of scoring 2 or fewer. Salah at 7.9 is the safer runner-up if that matters to you.

You are heavy on Arsenal and Manchester City: three players in one club and two in the other. That is the trade-off of picking from their strong seasons last year, and it means a bad day for either hurts more than it otherwise would.

Hold is the call. No transfer clears its cost against what you have, and you have a free one in the bank if something changes after Friday's team news or the early fixtures.

A hard note: every projection here comes from last season only. A player who started constantly then is projected as nailed now, but a summer move, a new manager or a lost starting berth would change that, and we do not see those yet. Watch for late squad news before you lock in.
